introduction_markdown: GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, General Certificate of Education Examination. 0760 HISTORY 1, JUNE 2022, ADVANCED LEVEL. Multiple choice question paper, One Hour 30 Minutes. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room. Instructions to candidates: use a soft HB pencil throughout the examination; do not open the booklet until told to do so; check that the question booklet is headed "Advanced Level - 0760 History 1". Answer ALL the 50 questions in this Examination. All questions carry equal marks. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Decide which answer is correct, find the number of the question on the Answer Sheet and draw a horizontal line across the letter to join the square brackets for the answer you have chosen. Mark only one answer for each question: if you mark more than one answer you will score a zero for that question. Avoid spending too much time on any one question; you can come back to it later. Do all rough work in the booklet, using, where necessary, the blank spaces in the question booklet.
incertitudes: Sujet scanné (CamScanner, filigrane gcerevision.com sans conséquence sur la lisibilité) de 5 pages : page de garde, puis 50 QCM sur les pages 2 à 5. Aucun corrigé officiel ni clé imprimée : toutes les réponses sont établies d'après l'historiographie courante (manuels camerounais et africains), sans source consultable pendant la transcription ; aucun chiffre ni date n'est avancé sans certitude.
Instructions de la page de garde : la numérotation imprimée saute de 10 à 12 (il n'y a pas d'instruction 11) ; recopié tel quel dans `introduction_markdown`.

Coquilles du sujet imprimé, conservées sauf mention : « Kovifen » (Q1, graphie du scan), « Fumbina » (Q3), « L'Effort Camerounaise » et « La Voix du people » (Q11), « Ucciali » (Q25), « Ramadier » (Q12). Deux coquilles évidentes ont été corrigées dans l'énoncé : « Minster » devenu « Minister » (option B de la Q18) et « Le Joir / Le Joiur » lu « Le Jour » (option C de la Q11, lecture du scan incertaine).

Q7 : le sujet écrit « West African Expeditionary Force » ; la force historique est la West African Frontier Force (avec les contingents français et britanniques de la campagne du Cameroun). Réponse retenue C (Douala, 27 septembre 1914), seule option correspondant à une première victoire alliée décisive ; Nsanakang est une défaite britannique.

Q9 : le sujet dit « Eastern Nigeria » pour la partie britannique du Cameroun ; en réalité le Southern Cameroons relevait de l'Eastern Region et le Northern Cameroons du Northern Region. L'option D (religious convenience) reste l'exception sans ambiguïté.

Q34 : l'option B (« economic crisis of the 2000s ») est un anachronisme (la guerre civile rwandaise date de 1990-1994) ; réponse B maintenue comme exception. Si l'examinateur a voulu écrire « 1980s », aucune option ne serait l'exception : à surveiller.

Q12, Q15, Q21, Q24, Q28 et Q50 : clé imprimée absente et options défendables à plusieurs titres (Q12 : les quatre options sont des parties de l'explication usuelle ; Q15 : options A et B quasi identiques et option D invérifiable ; Q21 : B, C et D sont toutes des moyens documentés ; Q24 : Algeciras 1906 et Congrès de Berlin 1878 sont tous deux hors sujet ; Q28 : la date de la Constitution Coussey (1950-51, non 1948) est inexacte dans le sujet ; Q50 : les quatre options sont des facteurs cités, seul « population density » est discutable). Elles ont été converties en questions ouvertes avec convertir_en_ouverte.js ; aucune lettre n'est choisie.

Réponses retenues avec un degré de certitude moyen (à relire par un historien avant mise en ligne) : Q1 D (Kapsiki est un peuple des monts Mandara, la nature des sites Pitti et Kovifen n'a pas pu être vérifiée), Q3 B (échec face au Mandara), Q4 B (fondation de Victoria en 1858), Q5 A (traités de protection et de commerce de la France avec des chefs côtiers, non documentés ici par un nom précis), Q6 A (plantations plutôt que routes et chemins de fer), Q11 D (titre de presse proche de l'UPC non vérifié ; les autres titres ne sont pas des titres UPC), Q14 C (justice coutumière de West Cameroon conservée ; les options A, B et D sont écartées avec certitude), Q16 D (conflits avec le Federal Inspector), Q17 B, Q19 C (les options A et B désignent la même unité d'élite, la Garde républicaine / présidentielle), Q23 D, Q30 C, Q31 A, Q33 B, Q35 A (C, augmentation de la population, est aussi un effet démographique et non strictement économique), Q37 D, Q39 D, Q47 C, Q48 A.

Les corrigés de ce sujet ne comportent ni citation, ni statistique, ni source inventée : les dates mentionnées (1858, 1884, 1914, 1961, 1972, 1975, 1984, etc.) sont celles de l'historiographie établie ; Q16 : Jua Premier ministre de West Cameroon en 1965, révoqué en 1968 ; Muna vice-président de la Fédération en 1970.
Converties en questions ouvertes par le relecteur (clé ou options discutables) : 12, 15, 21, 24, 28, 50. Aucune clé imprimée sur le sujet.

questions.enonce_markdown: The following ancestral sites were abandoned in the 19th century Cameroon due to population movements EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Pitti, Bankim and Kovifen (spelling as printed) are the places named in the traditions of the Tikar and Grassfields peoples as ancestral sites that were left behind when groups moved on during the 19th century, under pressure from raids and conquest and in search of land and security. Kapsiki is different in kind: it is the name of a people of the Mandara Mountains in the far north, not one of these vacated ancestral sites. It is therefore the exception.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A common characteristic of the states and kingdoms in the grasslands and coastal regions on the eve of European colonisation was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The question asks for what the grassland fondoms and the coastal chiefdoms had in common. In both zones the authority of the ruler (the Fon in the Grassfields, the chief or king on the coast) was balanced and enforced by **regulatory (secret or title) societies**: the Kwifon and similar societies in the Grassfields, the Ngbe (Ekpe) type of society on the coast. The Kwifon (B) and the Ahon (A) are particular institutions of particular peoples, and a council of elders (D) is a general feature of many African societies rather than the distinctive common institution of these two zones. The general category that fits both zones is regulatory societies.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A major setback to Modibo Adama's Jihad in Northern Cameroon was in:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Modibbo Adama led the Fulani jihad in the Fombina (Adamawa) region from the 1810s and built the emirate of Adamawa (capital Yola). The jihad subdued many peoples of the Adamawa plateau and its surroundings, so the Fombina/Adamawa campaign (A, D) was in general his success and not a setback. The Mandara kingdom, defended from its mountain base and its own army, was not conquered: the Mandara campaign is the usual example of a setback to the jihad.

**Answer: B.**
themes: fulani jihads in west africa and cameroon

questions.enonce_markdown: A manifestation of the imperial ambitions of the London Baptist Missionary Society on the coast of Cameroon was the:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Baptist missionary Alfred Saker, after the Spanish authorities expelled the Baptists from Fernando Po, founded **Victoria** in 1858 at Ambas Bay as a settlement for converts and freed people, named after the British queen and run on British lines. By creating a British-style colony-like settlement on the Cameroon coast the society showed ambitions that went beyond evangelisation. The Germano-Duala Treaty (A) was signed with Germany in 1884, not by the Baptist society; the withdrawal from Fernando Po (C) was a consequence of Spanish policy; mission stations (D) are the ordinary means of any missionary society.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A demonstration of France's determination to annex Cameroon in the 1880s was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the scramble for the coast, European powers staked their claims by signing treaties with local rulers. France's way of showing that it intended to take a share of Cameroon in the 1880s was to sign protective and trade agreements with some coastal chiefs. The scrapping of British courts (B) and the Cameroon Council (D) belong to the British and to the Duala side of the story, and the secret meetings with the Duala chiefs (C) are associated with the German approach that led to the treaty of July 1884.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: the signing of protective trade agreements with some coastal chiefs.
the scrapping of British courts in Cameroon.
the holding of secret meetings with Duala chiefs.
the setting up of the Cameroon Council.

questions.enonce_markdown: The Germans left an indelible economic legacy in Cameroon in the domain of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
German rule (1884-1916) was built on large plantations (cocoa, bananas, rubber, oil palm) around Mount Cameroon and the Victoria, Kumba and Moliwe areas, run by German companies. After 1916 these estates passed to the new administrations, and they became the basis of Cameroon's plantation economy, which still exists today. Roads and railways were also built, but they were designed to serve the plantations and trade, and the Central Line, for example, was only completed under French rule. Health and education (B, C) were left mostly to the missions. The most lasting economic legacy is plantation agriculture.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: the development of roads and railways.

questions.enonce_markdown: The first decisive victory of the West African Expeditionary Force during the First World War in Cameroon was in:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the Cameroon campaign of 1914-1916 the Allied (British and French) forces captured Douala, the German capital of the coast, which surrendered on 27 September 1914: this was the first decisive Allied victory. The Battle of Nsanakang (September 1914) was a British defeat; the German garrison at Mora held out until February 1916; Yaounde was taken only in January 1916, at the end of the campaign.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The main feature of Indirect Rule in the British Southern Cameroons during the Mandate period was that:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Indirect Rule meant governing through existing local rulers. In the Southern Cameroons the British organised traditional rulers and councils into **Native Authorities**, which collected taxes, kept order and ran native courts under the supervision of British officials. The other options are not the defining feature: the aim was cheap administration, not rebuilding institutions destroyed by the Germans or modernising them.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: traditional rulers were constituted into Native Authorities.
Southern Cameroons enjoyed the British system of justice.
it rebuilt indigenous institutions destroyed by the Germans.

questions.enonce_markdown: Britain administered her portion of Cameroon as an integral part of Eastern Nigeria because of the following EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Britain ran its Cameroons as part of Nigeria because it was cheap and easy: the territory was small and poor (financial convenience), it was next to Nigeria and had no separate administrative machinery (administrative convenience), and the two were geographically contiguous (geographical convenience). Religion played no part in the decision.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The French administration respected the following terms of the Mandate Agreement in French Cameroon EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
France sent annual reports to the League of Nations, maintained order and built roads and railways (notably the Douala-Yaounde line), as the Mandate required. It did not respect native laws and institutions: its policy was assimilation and direct rule, with chiefs reduced to auxiliaries and an indigenat regime of special penalties. The exception is therefore respect of native laws.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An influential UPC newspaper that educated the masses in French Cameroon against colonialism after 1945 was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Union des Populations du Cameroun (UPC), founded in 1948, used its press to explain its demands (independence and reunification) to the masses. Of the titles listed, Le Messager and Le Jour are not UPC titles, and L'Effort Camerounais is the title of a Catholic mission paper. The title that matches the UPC press is La Voix du Peuple (printed as "La Voix du people").

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The main reason for the fall of Andre-Marie Mbida from power as Prime Minister in 1958 was because:

*Options as printed:* A) he was dumped by Ahmadou Ahidjo.   B) he was disfavoured by Jean Ramadier.   C) he rejected immediate independence.   D) he refused to dialogue with the UPC.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Mbida, Prime Minister of French Cameroon from 1957, resigned in February 1958 and was replaced by Ahmadou Ahidjo. The accounts of his fall give several linked reasons: his refusal to ask France for immediate independence, his refusal to open a dialogue with the UPC, the withdrawal of the support of Ahidjo and the northern deputies, and the displeasure of the French High Commissioner, Jean Ramadier. Each of the four options is a part of that story, and the question does not say which one it takes to be the "main" one, so it cannot be marked as a single-letter question. A model answer would stress that Mbida lost the confidence of the Assembly and of France because he opposed the rapid move to independence and to a settlement with the nationalists.



The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The following were responsible for the victory of the KNDP in the 1961 Plebiscite EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the southern plebiscite of 11 February 1961 the voters could choose only between joining Nigeria and joining the Republic of Cameroon (no third option of independence), and the KNDP of John Ngu Foncha won the vote for joining Cameroon. Contributing factors usually given are the lack of an independence option (A), fear of domination by the Igbo and other Nigerians and other tribal feelings (B), and the unpopularity of Endeley's attitude (C). There is no evidence that the UN, which organised and supervised the plebiscite, falsified the results.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: the absence of the third option.
falsification of results by the UNO.

questions.enonce_markdown: An aspiration of the Southern Cameroonians respected by the 1961 Foumban Constitution was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Southern Cameroonians went to Foumban (July 1961) hoping for a loose federation, a federal capital that was not in the East, and a two-chamber legislature. The Federal Constitution gave them a strong central government (A is not met), set the federal capital at Yaounde (B), and created a single-chamber Federal National Assembly (D). What was kept was West Cameroon's own legal and judicial system with its customary courts, which the Constitution left in place.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: the seat of the Federal capital.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The following were political developments in East Cameroon that led to the creation of the CNU in 1966 EXCEPT:

*Options as printed:* A) Ahidjo's appeal for the creation of a Grand National Party.   B) Ahidjo's advocacy for a United Party.   C) the arrest and imprisonment of members of the Gang of Four.   D) the formation of a UC-UPC coalition government.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Cameroon National Union (CNU) was created in September 1966 when the parties of the federation merged into a single party under Ahidjo. In East Cameroon the steps leading to it were Ahidjo's calls for a single "national" or "united" party and the repression of opponents such as the leaders known as the Gang of Four. Options A and B describe the same call in two different wordings, and I cannot establish from the sources available that a UC-UPC coalition government (D) belongs or does not belong to this list, so no single option can be defended with certainty. The question is left open for self-assessment.



The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The main cause of the fall of A.N. Jua as Premier of West Cameroon in 1968 was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A.N. Jua became Prime Minister of West Cameroon in 1965 and was removed in 1968. The dismissal decree (A) is the act that removed him, not the cause; the unitary state came only in 1972 (B); and Muna became Vice President of the federation later, in 1970 (C). The underlying cause usually given is the repeated conflict between Jua's government and the Federal Inspector of Administration, the federal government's representative in West Cameroon.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: his opposition to the creation of a unitary system of government.
Ahidjo's decree appointing Muna as Vice President of the federation.
frequent clashes between Jua and the Federal Inspector.

questions.enonce_markdown: Between 1972 and 1982, Ahmadou Ahidjo's economic achievements in Cameroon were impressive in the field of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the last decade of Ahidjo's rule the most visible achievements were in infrastructure: the extension of the Transcamerounais railway to Ngaoundere (opened in 1974), the road programme and the development of ports and airports, which tied the north and the south of the country together. Agriculture, industry and housing grew much less impressively.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: President Ahmadou Ahidjo's achievement as an advocate of national unity in Cameroon was through the:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Ahidjo's main step towards national unity was the abolition of the federation and the creation of the United Republic of Cameroon, a unitary state, after the referendum of 20 May 1972. The restoration of the post of Prime Minister and his designation as constitutional successor (B, C) were later constitutional arrangements (1975) about the organisation of power and succession, not about unity, and D does not describe a unity measure.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: re-instatement of the post of Prime Minister.
making the Prime Minister his constitutional successor.
appointment of S.T. Muna to hold the posts of Prime Minister and Vice President.

questions.enonce_markdown: The April 6, 1984 Coup d'etat in Cameroon was abortive because of the role of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The coup of 6 April 1984 was launched by mutinous elements of the Republican (Presidential) Guard against President Biya. It failed after a few days of fighting because the forces that remained loyal to the President, the loyalist units of the army and the security forces, defeated the rebels. The Republican Guard and the Presidential Guard (A, B) are the elite guard units from which the rebels came, so they cannot explain the failure of the attempt; the Gendarmerie (D) was one component of the loyalist side, but the loyalist forces as a whole are what the question asks for.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The economic crisis in Cameroon in the mid 1980s can be attributed to the following EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The crisis that began in 1985-86 came from the fall in the world prices of Cameroon's exports (oil, cocoa, coffee), together with mismanagement, embezzlement and corruption, capital flight and heavy public spending. Falling prices of imported goods would have lowered the import bill and eased the situation; it is not a cause of crisis.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
A means by which the West African slave trading states were induced to stop the practice was:

*Options as printed:* A) Lord Mansfield's Court Decision in 1772   B) the use of diplomatic pressure.   C) payment of compensation.   D) signing of Equipment Treaties.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Lord Mansfield's decision of 1772 (the Somerset case) ruled on slavery inside England and did not act on the African slave-trading states, so A is not a means used on them. The other three were all used by Britain after 1807: diplomatic pressure and anti-slavery treaties with African rulers, subsidies or compensation paid to rulers for giving up the trade, and treaties with an equipment clause that allowed the navy to seize ships fitted for the slave trade. Because B, C and D each describe a documented means and the question does not say which one it has in mind, it is left open instead of being marked as a single-letter question. A model answer would explain the three means and add the blockade of the coast by the West Africa Squadron and the promotion of legitimate commerce.



The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: A long term positive political achievement of Christian missionary activities in West Africa was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The question asks for a long-term **political** achievement. Mission schools produced an educated African elite that learnt European languages and ideas of rights and self-government, and many nationalist leaders of West Africa came from this group: the missions thus laid the foundation for nationalism. Infrastructure (A) is economic, conversion (C) is religious, and the restoration of peace in Igboland (B) is neither a general nor a long-term political result.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A negative political impact of the Sokoto Jihad in Northern Nigeria was that:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Sokoto Jihad of Uthman dan Fodio (from 1804) created the Sokoto Caliphate, a theocratic state, and purified the practice of Islam, and it inspired later jihads such as that of Macina: these are generally presented as its positive or lasting results (A, B, C). Its negative political impact was the destruction of the old Hausa states and the lasting hostility and disunity it created between the Hausa states and Bornu, whose ruler opposed the jihad.

**Answer: D.**
themes: fulani jihads in west africa and cameroon

choix.texte: it led to the establishment of an Islamic theocratic state.
it led to the purification of Islam.
it inspired other Jihads in Macina and Futa Jallon.
it led to disunity in Hausaland and Bornu.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The following were reasons for the European scramble for and partition of Africa without war EXCEPT:

*Options as printed:* A) influence of the Berlin West Africa Conference.   B) influence of the Algeciras Conference.   C) influence of the Berlin Congress.   D) influence of the Brussels Conference.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The partition of Africa between about 1880 and 1900 took place without war between the European powers largely because of diplomatic meetings that set the rules for it: the Brussels Geographical Conference of 1876, which launched the interest in the Congo, and the Berlin West Africa Conference of 1884-85, which fixed the rule of effective occupation. The Algeciras Conference of 1906 dealt with Morocco after the partition was largely complete, so it cannot have been a reason for it. The Berlin Congress (1878) settled Balkan questions and is not usually counted among the conferences that governed the partition of Africa. Both B and C are therefore defensible as the exception and the question is left open instead of being marked as a single-letter question.



The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The Ethiopian victory over Italy at Adowa in 1896 could best be attributed to:
questions.corrige_markdown:
At Adowa (1 March 1896) the army of Emperor Menelik II destroyed the Italian force. The unpopularity of the war in Italy (A) was a consequence of the defeat rather than its cause; the mountainous terrain (B) helped but does not explain the victory alone; and the cancellation of the Treaty of Wuchale (Ucciali) (C) was the cause of the war, not of the victory. Menelik had united the country behind him, armed his army with modern rifles bought from European powers and used diplomacy and good intelligence: his military and political leadership is the best explanation.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: unpopularity of the war in Italy.
the cancellation of the Treaty of Ucciali.
effective military and political leadership of Menelik.

questions.enonce_markdown: The British policy of Indirect Rule in Africa was intended to accomplish the following EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Indirect Rule was meant to govern a large territory with few British officials by using African rulers, which reduced the cost of administration (A), made economic exploitation possible without resistance (B) and avoided conflict with the people (D). Recruiting African soldiers (C) was a separate military practice used under every system of colonial rule and was not an aim of Indirect Rule.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: reducing the cost of colonial administration.

questions.enonce_markdown: An outstanding social impact of the Second World War on the rise of African nationalism was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
African soldiers who fought in Europe, North Africa and Asia saw white soldiers defeated, afraid and wounded and fought beside them as equals: the **myth of white superiority** was destroyed, and this change of attitude was the major social effect that made Africans demand independence. The exhaustion of the colonial powers (A) is a political and economic effect, while urban growth (C) and trade unions (D) are consequences that helped nationalism but are less decisive.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: the exhaustion of colonial powers in World War II.
the destruction of the myth of white superiority.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The following were stages of decolonisation in the Gold Coast EXCEPT:

*Options as printed:* A) birth of the UGCC in 1947.   B) the rise of Nkrumah as secretary of the UGCC.   C) the Coussey Constitution of 1948.   D) the cutting down of cocoa trees.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The United Gold Coast Convention (UGCC) was founded in 1947 and Kwame Nkrumah became its general secretary, both clear stages on the road to independence. The cutting down of cocoa trees (the compulsory destruction of trees affected by swollen shoot disease) was a grievance of the farmers that fed discontent, rather than a political stage. The Coussey Committee was set up in 1948-49 after the Accra disturbances, and the constitution that followed dates from 1950-51, so the date printed in C does not match the usual dating. Because of this discrepancy the question is left open instead of being marked as a single-letter question: the most likely intended exception is D, the cutting down of cocoa trees.



The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The main economic reason for the Mau Mau Revolt in Kenya was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Mau Mau revolt (1952-1960) was led mainly by the Kikuyu, whose best land in the central highlands had been taken by white settlers. This **land alienation** left many Kikuyu landless or squatting as labourers and was the root economic grievance. Taxation, restrictions on African farming and compulsory terracing and contour farming were additional grievances, but secondary.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The Algerian War of Independence can be associated more with the activities of the 'Colons' because:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Colons were the European settlers of Algeria. They held the best land and most political power, refused any reform that would give Algerians equal rights, and treated Islam and Algerian culture with contempt. This attitude closed the legal road to change and pushed Algerians to armed struggle when the FLN began the war in November 1954. The other options concern Algerian actors (the educated elite, the nationalist movements) or the French policy of assimilation, not the behaviour of the Colons themselves.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: of dislike for the French policy of Assimilation.
of the influence of educated Algerian elite.
they despised Islam and destroyed Algerian culture.
of the activities of the nationalist movements.

questions.enonce_markdown: The main political manifestation of Neo-colonialism in former French Equatorial Africa is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Neo-colonialism means that a former colony is still controlled from outside after independence. In former French Equatorial Africa the clearest political sign is the set of defence and military agreements signed at independence, which kept French bases and allowed French troops to intervene in the internal affairs of these states. A presidential system modelled on France (B) and the French language (C) are legacies of colonial rule rather than control; D is not true, since French approval of cabinet reshuffles is not required.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: military conventions signed at independence still exist.
presidential system and constitutions are modelled on French pattern.
the French language is the official medium of communication.
cabinet reshuffles are subject to approval by France.

questions.enonce_markdown: The first military intervention in Nigeria led to the overthrow of the government headed by:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The first military coup in Nigeria took place on 15 January 1966 and overthrew the civilian federal government headed by Prime Minister Abubakar Tafawa Balewa, who was killed. General Aguiyi-Ironsi then took power as head of state; Azikiwe was the ceremonial President and Ojukwu was a military officer who led Biafra later.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An essential social motive of Apartheid in South Africa was the desire to:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Apartheid, applied from 1948, was justified by the claim that the races had to be kept apart to protect the white community: laws on mixed marriages, residential segregation and separate amenities were presented as protecting the racial purity and health of whites. This is the **social** motive. White minority rule (A) is political, and investments (C) and cheap labour (D) are economic motives.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: prevent the contamination of white race with diseases.
guarantee the supply of cheap black labour.

questions.enonce_markdown: The civil War in Rwanda was caused by the following EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The civil war in Rwanda began in 1990 with the invasion by the Tutsi-led RPF and ended in 1994. Its causes include ethnic rivalry between Hutu and Tutsi, the radicalisation of the exiled Tutsi (C, D) and the economic crisis of the late 1980s; the shooting down of President Habyarimana's plane in April 1994 was the immediate trigger of the genocide and of the last phase of the war (A). An economic crisis of the 2000s (B) came after the war and cannot have caused it.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: ethnic rivalry between the Hutu and Tutsi.

questions.enonce_markdown: The following were economic effects of the refugee crisis in Africa EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The arrival of large numbers of refugees raises the labour supply of host countries (B), increases the population and the demand for land, food and services (C) and forces governments to spend more on camps, health and security (D). Growing insecurity (A) is a social and political effect, not an economic one, and is therefore the exception.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: growing insecurity in the receiving countries.
boosting of the labour force of the host countries.
rapid increase in the population of receiving countries.
increase in government expenditure in the host countries.

questions.enonce_markdown: The Bill of Rights failed to satisfy all the aspirations of the English because:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Bill of Rights of 1689 limited the power of the Crown and confirmed the rights of Parliament, but it left the King's right of royal assent (a veto over legislation) and his large powers of patronage, and it did not reform the unrepresentative Parliament, so many demands remained unmet. The Habeas Corpus Act dates from 1679 (B), the Parliament was not elected too frequently (C), and the survival of James II in France (D) is not a defect of the Bill.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: James II was allowed to remain alive in France.

questions.enonce_markdown: A major factor that caused Britain to lose the American War of Independence was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
After the American victory at Saratoga (1777), France entered the war on the side of the colonies (1778), followed by Spain and the Dutch Republic. The French fleet and army made the decisive difference, notably at Yorktown (1781), where the British army was trapped and surrendered. The distance, the weak coordination of British operations and the cost of the war also counted, but foreign support is the factor that changed the balance.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: poor mastery of the American terrain.
poor planning and coordination of the war.
foreign support to the thirteen colonies.

questions.enonce_markdown: An outstanding European commitment of 1815 which gave birth to the Concert of Europe was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
After Napoleon's final defeat, Britain, Austria, Prussia and Russia renewed their alliance in the Quadruple Alliance of November 1815, and agreed to meet periodically to deal with European problems: this system of congresses is the Concert of Europe. The Holy Alliance (B) was a religious pledge of three monarchs, the Troppau Protocol (C) dates from 1820, and France joined the alliance, making it the Quintuple Alliance (D), only in 1818.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Bismarck's diplomatic skill was best demonstrated in the making of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Bismarck's aim after 1871 was to keep France isolated and to avoid war on two fronts. In 1887, when Austria and Russia were quarrelling over the Balkans, he signed the secret Reinsurance Treaty with Russia (each promised neutrality in some cases) while keeping Germany tied to Austria and Italy: reconciling these opposed commitments is the best proof of his skill. The other treaties (Dual Alliance 1879, Dreikaiserbund 1881, Triple Alliance 1882) are important, but simpler agreements.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The period from 28th June 1914 to 4th August 1914 can rightly be described as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
On 28 June 1914 Archduke Franz Ferdinand was assassinated at Sarajevo, and in the following weeks the ultimatum to Serbia, the declarations of war by Austria-Hungary, Germany, Russia and France and the German invasion of Belgium followed, until Britain declared war on Germany on 4 August 1914. These five weeks are the countdown to the outbreak of the war. The war itself lasted until 1918 (B), and the alliances were already formed before 1914 (D).

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: the countdown to the outbreak of the First World War.
the start and end of the First World War.
the peak of colonial rivalries in Africa.
the consolidation of alliances in Europe.

questions.enonce_markdown: At the Paris Peace Conference, the statement, 'I want a treaty which will cripple Germany and keep my country safe,' was the core aim of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Clemenceau, the French Prime Minister, wanted security for France against a new German attack: he asked for a weakened Germany (reduced army, loss of territory, reparations and the occupation of the Rhineland). Wilson wanted a peace based on the Fourteen Points and the League of Nations, Lloyd George wanted a compromise that would not ruin Germany, and Orlando was mainly interested in Italy's territorial claims.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The path to the collapse of the League of Nations in the 1930s began when:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The first great test of the League in the 1930s was the Japanese attack on Manchuria in 1931. The League condemned Japan but did nothing effective, and Japan left the League in 1933; this showed that aggression by a great power would go unpunished. The later events (Italy in Ethiopia in 1935, the Rhineland in 1936 and Spain from 1936) followed the same pattern.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Germany intervened in the civil war in Spain.

questions.enonce_markdown: The immediate cause of the outbreak of World War II was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939, and Britain and France, which had promised to defend Polish independence, declared war on Germany on 3 September. Isolationism, the collapse of collective security and appeasement are long-term causes that made the war possible.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The fundamental cause of the Cold War was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Cold War was a rivalry between the USA, defender of capitalism and liberal democracy, and the USSR, defender of communism; this ideological opposition is the root cause. Stalin's policy in Eastern Europe, the use of the atomic bomb in 1945 and Churchill's Iron Curtain speech (1946) are events that deepened the conflict.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: the use of the Atomic bomb.

questions.enonce_markdown: An important effect of the 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Cuban Missile Crisis of October 1962 brought the world close to nuclear war, and showed how slow communication between Washington and Moscow was. As a result a direct telephone and teleprinter link between the two leaders, the Hot Line, was set up in 1963. The overthrow of Batista (1959) and the Bay of Pigs (1961) came before the crisis, and the sugar boycott was part of the earlier quarrel with Castro.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: the overthrow of Batista by Fidel Castro.
the disgrace of the USA at the Bay of Pigs.
the boycott of Cuban sugar by the USA.
the establishment of the Hot Line.

questions.enonce_markdown: A conflict in the 1950s in which the USA used UNO as a tool of her foreign policy was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the Korean War (1950-1953) the Security Council, with the Soviet delegate absent in protest, authorised a UN force to defend South Korea; this force was in practice led and largely supplied by the USA. In the Suez crisis (1956) the USA acted differently, the Hungarian crisis (1956) did not lead to a UN force, and the Berlin Blockade (1948-49) was dealt with by the airlift.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The member states of the Commonwealth of Nations are united more by:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Commonwealth is a free association of states that were once part of the British Empire. They are held together mainly by the advantages that membership brings (trade links, aid, education and cooperation). Not all members have the Crown as head of state (B) and there is no common currency (D); equal status (A) is a principle of the association rather than the bond that keeps the members together.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: a common allegiance to the Crown.
the use of a common currency.

questions.enonce_markdown: The Arab states participated actively in the repeated Arab-Israeli Wars primarily because:
questions.corrige_markdown:
After the creation of Israel in 1948 the Arab states refused to recognise it and fought it in 1948, 1956, 1967 and 1973, with the declared aim of ending the Jewish state and recovering Palestinian and Arab land. Nasser (B) played a role in 1956 and 1967 but was not the root cause; Zionist solidarity (C) is the opposite side; and the West supported Israel, not the Arab states (D).

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: of the desire to destroy the state of Israel.
of the guarantee of Western support.

questions.enonce_markdown: A significant step towards peace in the Middle East was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Camp David Accords of September 1978, negotiated by President Carter between Egypt's Sadat and Israel's Begin, led to the Egypt-Israel peace treaty of 1979, the first peace between Israel and an Arab state. The Israeli withdrawal from Sinai (A) was a result of that treaty, while the UN resolutions and the ceasefires (C, D) have often not been respected.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: the withdrawal of Israel from the Sinai.
the signing of the Camp David Accord.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The following factors favoured China's emergence as a Third Force in World politics EXCEPT:

*Options as printed:* A) her huge population density   B) her huge natural deposits   C) Mao's victory over Chiang Kai-shek   D) improved Sino-American relations due to the Sino-Soviet Split.
questions.corrige_markdown:
China's rise as a power between the two blocs is usually explained by its very large population, its natural resources, the communist victory of Mao over Chiang Kai-shek in 1949, and the rapprochement with the USA that followed the Sino-Soviet split (Nixon's visit of 1972, entry into the UN in 1971). Each of the four options is cited in such accounts, so there is no clear exception: the printed "population density" is the only wording that is doubtful (the factor is the size of the population, not its density), but this is not enough to mark a single letter. The question is left open for self-assessment.



The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
